title: 金铲铲五年，如何成为自走棋赛道的“标准答案”？
event_sentences: 把每个新赛季，都当作“新品发布”
金铲铲上线时，自走棋的第一轮热潮已经过去。
上线以来，金铲铲常年稳居iOS畅销榜前列，最新“自然之力”赛季上线后更冲至畅销榜第二。
超过200种效果覆盖经济、棋子乃至商店机制，有些效果甚至能够永久改变弈子的形态。
《金铲铲之战》发行执行制作人叶菁此前接受采访时曾提到，项目组会把每一次赛季更新都当成一个新品来发布。
恭喜发财带来对弈爽感，双人模式让“铲搭子”有了更多合作空间，百人模式则进一步拓展了自走棋的竞技边界。
从麦当劳、海底捞，到乐刻等品牌合作，“开铲”开始出现在吃饭、社交、运动等生活场景里，逐渐融入年轻人的衣食住行。
五周年派对现场，一把超过2米高的巨大金色铲铲格外醒目，上面装饰着一把把由玩家亲手制作的小铲子。
今年五周年，金铲铲也把“启动”带到了公益场景中，为超过1500个留守儿童家庭送上AI阅读机器人。
这让“金铲铲启动”有了另一层含义：它不只是“上线玩一把”，也可以是一次主动出发，去给他人的生活添一点亮色。

title: TapTap在上海把玩家与创作者，“聚”在了一起
event_sentences: 其次是现场还准备了相当丰富的游戏试玩内容：包括《控制：共振》这样的待上线国外买断制单机大作（值得一提的是，本次玩聚节是《控制：共振》在国内首次面向普通玩家开放试玩），还有《白银之城》这样高关注度的未上线国产游戏，而8月刚在成都和科隆办完两场大规模线下试玩会，并获得科隆游戏展「最具史诗感」大奖的《湮灭之潮》，这次也把试玩版本带到了玩聚节。
比如《控制：共振》的执行制作人Juha Vainio在现场提到IP新作是Remedy首次花费大量资源在玩法上；《inZOI》制作人金亨俊则在现场首次公开了游戏的新UGC功能“Canvas Town”（画布小镇）。
其次是一些精品独立游戏，比如在国内拥有很高人气的《泰拉瑞亚》，其主创团队首次来到中国与国内玩家见面，现场还公布了游戏最新版本的更新内容；双点工作室创始人Gary Carr和Mark Webley在现场正式公布了《双点博物馆》的全新DLC；《苏丹的游戏》制作人远古之风则分享了自己将游戏从PC端移植到手游端的心路历程；《鬼谷八荒》制作人张三则首次带来了《鬼谷八荒2》的消息，表示新作的“体量”会很大。
可以发现，这些创作者除了在现场分享创作理念与创作故事外，还会选择将一些游戏的最新动向，也在现场进行发布。
比如首次来到中国的《泰拉瑞亚》主创，就在本次玩聚节与国内玩家们来了一次双向奔赴，现场放出了一条国内玩家集体制作的VCR，记录了许多国内玩家在《泰拉瑞亚》中渡过的美好回忆。
事实上，基本上每一位来到现场的开发者，都会在QA环节回答国内社区玩家的问题，甚至还有一些问题是通过现场互动小游戏的形式进行，比如《inZOI》制作人金亨俊在现场与玩家一起游玩的“人生选择”小游戏，其中就提到了一个与游戏开发息息相关的问题——是为打磨功能推迟更新，还是按照原计划发布未完成的版本？
TapTap的0分成政策对于抗风险能力较弱的独游开发者来说也更加友好，开发者可以没有负担地登陆TapTap。
但是海外开发者的主要问题在于不够熟悉中国游戏市场，尤其是没有与国内专业发行商合作的海外开发者，他们一方面需要打开国内市场，另一方面哪怕是一些已经具备较高全球知名度的产品，也需要与国内玩家建立更加直接的联系，做好国内市场的运营工作。
而传统的PC主机买断制游戏，其产品特性决定了研发周期较长较封闭，所以开发团队往往是在产品重要节点，举行发布会/试玩会等活动。
在产品正式上线以后又不像GaaS游戏那样会高频更新，持续与玩家产生互动。
而TapTap在上线PC版以后，能够将自己的玩家社区生态能力也迁移到PC端，这就补齐了PC游戏开发者的这部分需求，并且由于TapTap本身包含了大量移动游戏用户，在TapTap主动打通PC端与移动端生态用户，这些手游玩家还有可能迁移到PC平台，成为PC游戏的增量用户。
具体来说，在新游上线前的预热阶段，TapTap会提供游戏预约、测试资格发放等等，开发者也可以早早地入驻TapTap，提前培育自己的社区生态。
而到了首发期，TapTap也会有展示位推荐，热门榜单等发行资源来为新游上线提供助力；最后是当产品步入长线运营期以后，TapTap的版本更新汇总、玩家社区、内容生态、反馈与沟通机制等一系列能力，又能帮助GaaS游戏开发者更好地维持产品的长线生命力。
从这次玩聚节的GaaS游戏阵容中也能发现，既有《白银之城》这样未上线的游戏，也有《王者万象棋》这样刚刚上线的游戏，还有《明日方舟》这种运营多年的成熟产品。
在行业内很多人眼中，TapTap一直有点像是一个“理想主义者”，毕竟在TapTap选择0分成政策的时候，国内游戏行业关于“渠道为王”还是“内容为王”的争论正值高峰，TapTap能够在当年作下这个决定，是一件相当具有勇气的事情。

Hive团队庆祝创作的地图被游玩超过10亿次

对于小型团队而言，在项目刚上线、费用较低时提前进行商标布局或许是防范风险的唯一手段，但矛盾的是往往许多创作者在项目尚未验证成功前，根本没有这样的知识产权保护意识。

title: 腾讯不要的团队做出爆款：《Wardogs》Steam首日34万在线、服务器挤爆
event_sentences: GameLook报道/一边是销量喜报，一边是服务器事故，英国工作室Bulkhead大概很难忘记《WARDOGS》上线的这一天。
9月10日，这款由Team17发行的FPS开启Steam抢先体验，当天累计销量先是突破100万份，随后又迅速报到125万份，Steam同时在线峰值达到34万人。
而就是这样一款讲究三方混战的产品，正式上线之前，《WARDOGS》已经热得让开发者有些招架不住。
Bulkhead的CEO Joe Brammer当时在社交媒体上忍不住喊道：“为什么你们有25000人跑进靶场？
到了最后一轮测试，游戏同时在线人数进一步冲到了24.5万人。
9月5日，官方宣布把封闭测试转为开放测试，招呼玩家“来把我们的服务器搞崩”。
谁能想到，这句话到了上线当天，竟然成了最贴切的预告。
前期测试已经聚集了几十万人，正式发售却又迎来一波更猛烈的冲击，开发者期待的大战场盛况，首先出现在了登录界面。
对玩家来说，149元已经付了，能不能进游戏比百万销量重要得多。
2022年，腾讯旗下Splash Damage收购了Bulkhead；到了2025年末，它又被出售，由SMG、Team17母公司Everplay及Hiro Capital组成的财团接手。
腾讯曾经握着这张牌，只是在它真正打出百万销量之前，已经把牌交到了别人手里。
公司会考虑自己能给合作带来什么、双方的长期方向是否匹配，以及独立是否能让团队获得更好的发展机会。
再看回报，125万份销量若按39.99美元美区标价粗算，就是接近5000万美元的销售规模。
即便给区域定价和渠道分成留出空间，对照当初1000万至1200万英镑的预算，《WARDOGS》也很可能在上线第一天，就把研发成本赚了回来。

title: 失业后自学游戏引擎，他一人用AI做游戏，在Steam新品节打败八成对手
event_sentences: 人与AI相互理解，或许是未来开发游戏的最佳状态 。
AI拯救了失业中年人
80%的Steam新品节游戏，愿望单数量居然被一款完全用AI做的挂机游戏打败，这合理吗？
失业后，40多岁的老刘决定重新拾起游戏梦，他没有游戏经验，也不懂编程，更惨的是 ， 他的第一款游戏做了4年还没上线。
但今年的转机出现在他第一款真正做完的AI游戏里 —— 仅靠一个Demo，首周就从新品节收获了近3000个愿望单，从4200款游戏中突围，这个成绩已经相当难得。
22年失业后，老刘花2个月的时间做了一段游戏概念视频，这是他第一次尝试立项，目标是做出一款高精度的虚幻5横板冒险游戏， 且要 包含解密、旅行、经营等玩法要素 。
这吸引 了不少期待游戏上线的玩家。
不过 这「失败」的四年时光， 让 老刘积攒了不少对游戏画面、光影、关卡设计的理解， 这些 成了他后来用AI做游戏最核心的竞争力。
毕竟， AI能轻松帮他生成代码、图片、音乐和素材，但并不能判断哪种游戏画面是好看的、什么关卡是设计合理的。
但过去四年的积累，决定了他能补足哪些AI做不到的事情。
让AI做95%的工作，
不用亲自写代码，整个游戏几乎是老刘和AI“聊”出来的。
刚 开始做《后日时光》的时候，老刘还是会把AI当成传统开发工具来用，流程一般是由他负责设计蓝图，AI则负责代码实现。
但很快问题就出现了，一旦程序出BUG，老刘既看不懂代码，也不知道AI改了哪里，最后本该用来开发游戏的时间与精力，大部分都用来排查与修复BUG。
老刘也 曾尝试过让AI将蓝图翻译成代码、并统一用语逻辑，但效果并不见得有多好。
开发工具的转变，让 老刘 手工和AI协作 的比例 从虚幻5时期的50:50，变为了后来使用Godot的5：95。
“ 要学会让AI当主创 ，而不是当助手。
”老刘在自己另一个账号@老刘用AI做游戏 的 视频内 ， 说 过 这 样一 段话 。
很多 人用AI创作的常规思路是，先告诉AI，自己要做A、B和C，那么AI就会按照自己的方式实现ABC；但老刘的做法是，他会问AI：“如果我想要直接达成E的话，剩下的ABCD该怎么设计一套高效的执行计划？
除了核心内容设计，老刘在选题阶段就会让AI占据主导权，自己作为制作人只负责判断和取舍 。
得益于此，他最后 锁定了挂机陪伴的赛道， 因为 这类游戏只需做好番茄钟功能并以挂机为主要玩法设置养成线路，再利用AI做好视觉资源的堆料 。
后来发现AI比想象中还要全能，老刘就开始“得寸进尺”：问能不能给播放器加个Lo-Fi滤镜？
AI它说能。
AI说它能。
AI说它也能 ……
但 老刘在 用 AI 做 游戏的开发中，看到了另一种 既 保留个人风格 ，又 低成本高效率完善项目模块的可能性。
事实证明，AI实现的效果可圈可点 ， 甚至让 自己也学到了一套在2D环境下控制全局光影的方法论。
在《旅行家：后日时光》demo发布前，老刘没有为游戏做过长周期的预热，只是简单地在自媒体发布了demo上架的相关动态。
按他的预期来看，并不指望这种“摆烂式”的游戏上线方式能带来多少流量，毕竟它的Steam页面简介上还写着“这是一款绝佳的学习陪伴游戏，因为它不好玩”。
聊到AI， 老刘给我们讲了另一个开发者的故事 ：
有一位他认识的AI游戏开发者， 最初产品“AI味” 比 较重，且玩法上没有亮点，发到外网还被reddit玩家吐槽“看不到人为打磨的痕迹”。
这 其实 说明了一件事，AI制作 的游戏能保持项目的基础质量下限，但作品上限还是取决于开发者的审美，以及对于 什么 游戏“有卖相”这一点的判断能力。
抖音的互动空间、B站的Toy、小红书的vibe coding …… 如今各家内容平台掀起AI小游戏的制作热潮，AI游戏的开发未来将更加下沉，AI游戏开发再也不全是懂行者来掌局。
老刘对此的评价是：随着制作门槛的下放与功能实现流程的简化，AI游戏可能会迎来自己的“短视频”时代，未来会出现1到5分钟就能玩完的快节奏“短游戏”，这些“短游戏”则会成为新型的引流入口。
可以说，全民皆为AI兵的景象并不是一种空想。
回顾游戏史，曾经有不少火爆的新游戏类型都来自社区：反恐精英系列起源于半条命的Mod、绝地求生的诞生可以追溯到武装突袭3模组、曾因为归属权问题而让Valve和暴雪大打出手的Dota，原先只是一张魔兽争霸3的社区地图...... 而现在 ，AI让游戏创作的成本更低， 甚至 下一个革新行业的产品，也许不需要先诞生在一家游戏公司里 。
包括前不久 ，OpenAI发布的最新前沿模型GPT-6 Astra横空出世。
最后老刘感叹道，个人用AI做3D游戏的时代已经来临了。
他提到，曾经自己收到过 知名AI Agent公司 的 offer， 对方 开出一定的待遇条件，希望能邀请他 去 负责开发游戏模型。
《旅行家：后日时光》游戏Demo对于老刘最大的意义，从来不是那3000多个愿望单的数量， 甚至 不是在发售后能带来多少销量 ， 而是他对AI有了更深度的认识：以前不逼着自己去深度使用，会低估AI的作用上限； 可如今 用了半年之后， 他发现 原来还会卡住自己的开发痛点，回过头来早已能够另辟蹊径去攻克了。
而老刘也像游戏内 的 主角一样，在旅途中不断积累着经验与资源，怀揣着独特的AI游戏开发愿景 ， 走向下一个 职业 生涯 的 节点。
发布于：北京市

title: 64家游戏公司半年报：薪酬成本下降9亿，亏损的公司翻了一倍
event_sentences: 64家公司的整体游戏收入仅增长9%，增速腰斩，如果去掉腾讯，整体营收更是堪堪维稳。
文末附本期财报的营收、利润，以及各项成本总表。
需要说明的是，薪酬成本包含工资、奖金、股份支付、五险一金等福利开支，也包含离职补偿和减员开支，它的高低不直接等于员工的实际待遇，但能部分反映公司的用工成本水平。
其中涨得最多的是家乡互动和巨人网络，增幅都超过40%。
一是离职补偿，公司员工数从期初的564人降到期末的355人，降幅 为 37%；二是以股份为基础的开支大幅增加，从上期的264万元涨到本期的2478万元，增幅 达 839%。
中手游薪酬成本下降， 主要因为整体营收同比下滑53%，同期在职人数减少约50%，另外 他们去年还有 一笔一次性裁撤补偿抬高了去年的成本基数。
变动方面，家乡互动的人均薪酬成本涨了超过100%，除了上文提到的总薪酬成本增长 外 ，公司人数还 少 了37%，两项叠加导致人均 数据 大幅上涨；
贪玩的人均薪酬成本降了超过40%，原因是贪玩2025下半年招了不少人，员工数从958人涨到 了 1239人 。
需要说明的是，为了保证数据口径统一和具备可对比性，分母统一用期初期末平均员工数，分子分别用公司整体营收和归母净利润，所以部分公司的数据会受非游戏业务影响。

title: 恺英网络参股娱美德，传奇IP权属重构在即
event_sentences: 公告表示,恺英网络拟通过全资香港子公司Cypress Technology HK Limited收购Neosphere Co., Limited（以下简称“Neosphere”）49%股权，而Neosphere间接全资子公NeoPulse正是此前公布拟收购娱美德39.33%股份并成为其新任第一大股东的主体。
从早年和世纪华通业务合作，到购买世纪华通股票升级为股权合作，再到2026年2月，恺英网络全资子公司上海恺英与株式会社传奇 IP 签署《和解协议》，了结持续已久的仲裁争端。
不同于行业常见的对抗式维权，恺英网络选择以和解的方式寻求多方共赢，这也为后续更进一步的资本合作搭建起信任基础。
股权易主带来产业格局重构窗口，恺英网络顺势推进间接参股娱美德，把合作从业务层面上升到资本层面，进一步实现角色跃迁。
而进入移动互联网时代后，《传奇》系列游戏走向移动化，长期占据畅销榜榜首，最高月流水近7亿，成为当年最成功的手游之一。
伽马数据显示，2025 年传奇 IP 市场规模达到 355.5 亿元，多年稳定维持 300 亿以上级别；截至 2025 年末 IP 已累计创造价值超 3700 亿元，机构预判 2026 年市场规模有望突破 400 亿元，仍具备巨大潜力。
此次资本合作，有利于从根源改善授权乱象，实现对被授权主体、产品内容、运营行为的整体把控，有效保护玩家权益与正版厂商利益，为传奇 IP 生态闭环筑牢制度基础。
公司将积累海外上市公司股东治理、跨境股权投资实操经验，提升在传奇全产业链的角色定位，同时为未来对接更多海外IP资源建立合作范本。

title: 独立创作者借AI发力，TapTap热门榜前十闯入3款“AI制作”游戏
event_sentences: AI游戏正在成为平台上的一股新流量。
近日，《军旅》、《古玩人生》、《崇祯直聘：明末官场沉浮模拟器》等多个由个人制作的AI游戏进入TapTap热门前十。
近期网易也上线了一款名为“星匣”的AI游戏创作产品，入口目前设置在LOFTER内。
该产品暂未进行大规模宣发，预估仍处于小范围测试阶段，主要通过手机端应用广告推流的方式引流。
结合目前TapTap头部榜单几款产品来看，模拟经营和文字模拟器成为AI游戏较为集中的落地方向。
值得注意的是，大部分登上榜单的 AI 游戏制作团队普遍极小，不乏单人团队。
能够从评论看出，大部分玩家鲜少对AI生成的游戏文案挑剔，最多是质疑内容的合理性。
其次，AI编程工具进一步降低了玩家做游戏的成本 。
OpenAI近期发布的GPT-6 Astra，已经展示了从自然语言需求直接生成可玩游戏、修改代码，并通过工具参与测试和迭代的能力。
B站UP主守望星空はは近日发布了“一句话做《穿越火线》”的视频，虽然只有短短的30秒，但已经实现了购买枪支、开镜、切刀、击杀敌人等基本功能，甚至敌人还有行为逻辑，最基本的枪支音效也已经实现。
他在视频中留言说，现在一个小白，只要会打字，就能够开发游戏；随后补充，他做出这个游戏总共消耗10亿token，让AI从网上搜集素材而不是从零制作，可以大大减少用量，并且加快速度。
过去一个人做游戏，最难的就是与人合作这一关。
现在，开发者可以用AI补代码、生成界面和批量扩写事件，把数周甚至数月的原型期压缩到几天之内。
但这并不意味着AI已经能完整替代游戏开发：大部分的开发者抱怨，有了AI之后，自己的时间没有变得充裕，反而感觉休息更加奢侈——“AI替我承担了大部分的工作，可是决策成本依旧由我自己承担”。
同时，AI生成3D游戏仍有不少需要改进的空间。
大部分3D独立游戏在Steam上有很多差评的主要原因，就是测试开发不足导致的BUG太多；
在角色、场景和商业级资产制作上，开发者往往仍要搭配Tripo等垂直AI生成3D工具，以及相关建模软件完成后续修整。
AI辅助游戏开发目前更常见的做法，仍是“人工设计主循环以及系统+AI生成局部内容”的混合形态。
它没有先做传统应用商店，而是把AI创作入口放进LOFTER这类已有同人、小说和角色创作人群的社区里，让用户既是玩家，也是作者。
B站也发布了互动内容发布平台Toy。
根据官方简介，UP主可以上传测试、小游戏等内容，用户无需跳出B站或者下载APP，点击链接可以直接体验。
与此同时，B站也举办了“Build in Bilibil AI创造公开赛”，鼓励UP主使用AI完成产品开发，并且录制相关开发视频上传。
抖音也有“互动空间广场”，主要借助字节旗下AI开发工具Trae完成作品制作。
不光如此，快手也在启动首批AI创作者招募。
其中动作最明显的还是小红书，自从“小工具”公测以来，不少创作者将自己的静态Html作品可以直接挂载到笔记下面，平台本身倒是没有内卷AI开发工具，而是提供作品容器和流量入口。
根据近期行业报道，小红书公布的Vibe Coding作品榜Top 10一度有7款休闲游戏，《烤肉模拟器》使用人数超过60万。
《开蚌直播间：稀有珍珠由你开》的使用人数也超过40万。

title: 暴雪嘉年华：“魔兽世界2”、星际IP开放世界射击游戏、暗黑5全来了
event_sentences: 这是微软收购动视暴雪之后首届线下暴雪嘉年华。
此外，由Netflix制作的《暗黑破坏神》动画剧集已正式立项开发；《暗黑 4》新赛季“炼狱遗产赛季”，亚马逊职业包将于2027上半年上线。
不难看出，《魔兽世界：无限》的立项初衷，是在延续经典旧世风味的前提下，重铸魔兽故事线，继续开拓60级版本内容，并持续将其运营下去。

title: Has the "Content" Cycle in the Anime and Manga World Come to an End?
event_sentences: At the recent Gamescom in Cologne, miHoYo unveiled *The Origin’s Knot*, a title that feels very “un-miHoYo-like.” After our colleagues on the ground had a chance to try it out, they were pleasantly surprised by the level of detail in its realistic visuals and the cooperative PVE design, which conveyed a distinct vibe different from miHoYo’s usual style.

But every paradigm has its limits,Today, the cost of content production continues to rise with each new release, the supply of characters is nearing the tipping point of aesthetic fatigue, and increased investment in content no longer automatically translates to better commercial returns. As these various signals converge, finding a new strategic foothold for anime and manga products is no longer merely a strategic choice for individual companies—it has become a challenge that any company entering this category must inevitably face.
I think that’s right—there will never be another successful product like Genshin Impact or Mingchao again.

In my view, miHoYo’s *The Origin’s Knot* remains a “content-driven product”—a content-based game that doesn’t rely on a specific aesthetic niche and is aimed at a broader global player base. Who says gameplay isn’t content?

As I understand it, “content” is actually a methodology—starting with character design → plot and presentation → promotional videos to build anticipation → monetization through gacha releases → and maintaining engagement until the next character is introduced. Based on this methodology, the entire team structure, production schedule, user expectation management, and business model of previous anime-style products were all built around this cycle.

The advantage of the latter approach is that, once the core mechanics are in place, the production costs for subsequent content can be kept relatively under control. This is also one of the reasons why investors and management are beginning to shift their focus toward gameplay—not solely because a “gameplay-oriented approach is better,” but also because it offers a healthier cost structure.
For most other “high DAU” games focused on gameplay, emotional investment comes from other players.
So my assessment is that in the coming years, we’ll see a wave of hybrid products where “gameplay is the backbone and content is the flesh”—it won’t be a one-sided affair.

Whether it’s “The Primordial Knot” or “Infinity,” rather than abandoning content, it’s more accurate to say they’re rebalancing the ratio between content and gameplay. Similar trends can be seen in newer titles with a stronger anime-style aesthetic, such as “Blue Starfield,” “Silver City,” and “Sleepless Wilderness”—characters remain important, but they are no longer the sole pillar of the game.
When people discuss whether the anime and manga boom has come to an end, they’re actually sidestepping a more fundamental question: How many companies in this industry have actually made money?

The core contradiction of the content model lies in the fact that it requires an extremely high upfront investment to build content barriers, yet its monetization model—namely, character-based payments—is inherently limited by the size of the core anime and manga user base. You might spend a fortune creating a top-tier open world, but the pool of players willing to pay for characters may be quite small.

Companies like Mihoyo and Eagle Corner have succeeded because they’ve built up a user base, content capabilities, and technical infrastructure in this genre—things that money can’t buy. Many latecomers attempt to achieve the same results through rapid capital investment, which is, in itself, a misjudgment.
Every two years, the industry comes up with a new narrative to explain why the previous generation of products failed.

The year before last saw user acquisition reach its peak; last year saw a shakeout in the anime and manga sector; and this year, it’s the “end of the content cycle” all over again. In another two years, once this batch of new games—touting “gameplay-driven” approaches—launches and flops spectacularly, there will likely be yet another buzzword.
I think everyone needs to understand this: Products with great content are still profitable today, while products with poor gameplay will still fail in the future.
Instead of agonizing over whether to focus on content or gameplay, it’s better to start by answering a more fundamental question: Is what you’re creating actually any good?

There is one issue we must face head-on: globally successful gameplay-driven games almost never use the F2P model; the mainstream models are buy-to-play or a one-time payment plus DLC. Yet what Chinese teams excel at most is precisely the long-term operation of F2P games.

This is where the next generation of anime and manga-inspired products will truly be put to the test—not whether they can create engaging gameplay, but whether they can develop a sustainable business model based on that gameplay while moving away from the “Gach” model.

title: Kaiying has indirectly invested 2.1 billion yuan in Yumede, which holds 80% of the revenue from the Legend IP license.
event_sentences: This evening (the 12th), Kaiying Network issued an announcement stating that it plans to indirectly hold approximately 19.7% of the shares in South Korea’s WeMade.

Kaiying partnered with a Hong Kong-based platform to establish an SPV (special purpose vehicle). Through a series of complex transactions, it acquired a 39.33% stake from WeMade’s founder for $608 million. Combined with the 0.92% stake it already held,it now holds approximately 40.25% of WeMade’s equity, making it WeMade’s largest shareholder. Kaiying holds a 49% stake in the SPV and, after looking through the structure, indirectly holds approximately 19.7% of WeMade’s equity.

The transaction values Yumedia at approximately 2.34 trillion won (about 10.3 billion yuan), with a price per share of 68,910 won—3.6 times the closing price of 19,330 won on the date the agreement was signed and 6 times its book net asset value.Kaiying is investing $298 million in this acquisition, equivalent to approximately 2.1 billion yuan.

On June 30, the founder of WeMade officially announced the sale of his shares, with a mysterious Chinese investor taking over the company. At the time, the media’s first reaction was to wonder whether Century Huatong was involved. After all, since Century Huatong holds the exclusive mainland China licensing rights to the “Legend” IP, it was the most logical assumption.

However, Century Huatong immediately denied the reports, stating that the acquisition had nothing to do with the company.South Korean media also reported that the CEO of the acquiring party had close ties to Alibaba and that Alibaba personnel had assisted in the negotiations. Coupled with recent reports that Alibaba was selling Lingxi Interactive Entertainment, the identity of the buyer remained a mystery for a time. Two and a half months later, Kaiying revealed the answer in an official announcement.

In its announcement, Kaiying stated that the investment in WeMade aims to deepen its strategic partnership with the original rights holder of *Legend of Mir*, secure domestic adaptation and distribution rights for *Legend of Mir* mobile games, browser games, and H5 games, and expand into overseas markets through WeMade’s listing platform in South Korea.The terms of the transaction stipulate that the SPV will use its best efforts to enter into a licensing agreement with WeMade at a price no higher than that specified in the existing licensing agreement, and will then license the “Legend” IP to a party designated by Kaiying.

According to Gamma Data, the market size of the “Legend” IP is projected to reach 35.55 billion yuan in 2025, having remained stable at around 30 billion yuan for several consecutive years. The long-standing chaos caused by multiple licensing agreements has made “securing control over the source of copyrights” a crucial step.

For WeMade founder Park Kwan Ho, this was a way to break free from his financial constraints. He had previously pledged approximately 65% of his shares to 16 financial institutions, borrowing about 93 billion won, with multiple pledge agreements maturing in July and August of this year.WeMade posted a net loss of approximately 27 billion won in 2025, with its profits relying almost entirely on licensing fees from China. This, combined with the delisting of the WEMIX token from exchanges, has severely impacted the company’s ability to service its debt. Selling the shares at a 3.6-fold premium allows the company to avoid forced liquidation.
Disputes over the ownership of “Legend” IP in mainland China have a long history but have gradually been resolved in recent years.

In 2023, Yataos, a subsidiary of Century Huatong, acquired the exclusive mainland China rights to the Legend IP for a total of 500 billion won over five years.In 2025, a South Korean court confirmed an 80:20 revenue-sharing arrangement between WeMade and Atoos. By February 2026, Kaiying had reached a settlement with Legend IP, and by June, it had finalized royalty settlements with Atoos, effectively eliminating litigation risks and paving the way for this equity investment.

title: A small studio that was "abandoned" by Tencent created a smash hit generating over 340 million yuan in daily revenue.
event_sentences: It’s hard to believe that, even in 2026, there are still multiplayer games that subject players to the nightmare of queuing—and *Wardogs*, a large-scale battlefield shooter released today, has achieved the “feat” of having 330,000 players waiting in line online.

In fact, even before its official release, the game already showed signs of becoming a hit. During the closed beta alone, *War Dog* attracted nearly 250,000 players, and during the pre-order period, it quickly climbed to the top of Steam’s global best-seller list.According to an official announcement, *War Dog* sold 1.25 million copies on its first day of release. Based on a pre-order price of $40, the game generated nearly $50 million (approximately 335 million RMB) in revenue on its first day.

Interestingly, this “small studio” from Derby, England, has had a long-standing connection with Tencent.In 2020, Tencent spent a massive $1.3 billion to acquire Leyou Technologies and its subsidiary studio, Splash Damage. Then, in 2022, Splash Damage acquired Bulkhead, the developer of *War Dogs*. At the time, Tencent held an indirect stake in Bulkhead, and *War Dogs* was officially greenlit shortly thereafter.

However, the honeymoon period was short-lived. In September 2025, Tencent sold Splash Damage to the private equity firm Emona Capital. Although the Bulkhead project had been “recognized” by Tencent at the time and was spun off to remain within the company, such a small company could never satisfy the appetite of a corporate giant.Before long, Bulkhead’s management established a new holding company, SMG, and formed a consortium with Everplay and Hiro Capital to acquire Bulkhead in its entirety from Tencent, ultimately succeeding in “buying their freedom.”

Joe Brammer, founder and CEO of Bulkhead, later recalled: “In 2022, our first year of partnership with Tencent, it truly felt like a dream come true.They said, ‘Hey, we’ve got a lot of funding here—go create something, and then tell us what product you’ve built and who you want to sell it to.’ That was the period when we achieved the most.”

At the time, the production budget for *War Dogs* ranged from 10 to 12 million pounds, which was already a huge step forward for a small studio; however, Tencent hoped the studio would achieve even greater success.

In Joe Brammer’s view, the project Tencent had in mind was simply too large-scale for them. After all, they had previously started out as a team of just five people and had developed only three titles before *War Dog*,two puzzle games, *Pneuma: Breath of Life* and *The Turing Test*, and their best-selling shooter, *Battalion 1944*, which had sold only 580,000 copies—yet Tencent’s goal at the time was a blockbuster with a budget of 50 million pounds.

Joe Brammer explained: “Between 2021 and 2022, Tencent conveyed the following message to all UK developers: they would not consider any project with an investment cost below 50 million pounds.As a result, Tencent sometimes wondered why we invested so little in the *War Dog* project. Although we met all our objectives, the investment amounted to only 50 percent of what was originally planned—a product of this scale was clearly not what Tencent was looking for.”

In 2025, Tencent began deliberately divesting and reviewing its overseas investment assets. For Bulkhead, the issue may not have been that the product wasn’t good enough, but rather that its scale simply didn’t fit into Tencent’s strategic plans.Yet this passive “breakup” actually granted *War Dog* an unimaginable degree of freedom: the team did not publish a content update roadmap, did not include any in-app purchases, and focused solely on game optimization, balance adjustments, and bug fixes during the Early Access period—as well as addressing any issues raised by players after they started playing. True content updates would not begin until after the official 1.0 release.
Despite making a series of seemingly outlandish promises, *War Dogs* still managed to have its moment in the spotlight after its release.

On this massive map, a fixed “control zone” measuring 2×2 kilometers will spawn randomly. The players’ objective is to have as many members as possible within this control zone. The faction with the most members in the zone will control the entire area and earn 1 point after a certain period of time. The first faction to reach 100 points wins the game.
As I mentioned earlier, this game has no in-app purchases, but it still includes a variety of skins and items. The resource used to obtain these rare items is called “gold bars.”

There are only two ways to obtain gold bars: one is to purchase them directly with money, but exchange rates fluctuate significantly, so “invest with caution.” For example, when I first started playing the game, one bar cost only 200,000, but after finishing a match, the price skyrocketed to over 2.7 million.

Like *Battlefield*, *War Dogs* features numerous soldier classes, but these classes cannot be freely selected before entering the game; instead, players must perform various actions within the game to earn the corresponding experience.For example, killing enemies earns Assault experience, while rescuing players earns Medical experience. All experience is aggregated into a personal level, which unlocks corresponding items and firearms.It’s worth noting that these class levels and experience points are not reset with version updates but are permanently retained. This means that the more time players invest, the stronger they will become in the game.

In terms of equipment complexity, *War Dog* falls somewhere between *Battlefield* and *Escape from Tarkov*—you don’t have to manually load rounds into magazines, but you still need to plan your resource allocation wisely based on your backpack’s capacity.Standard gear—including helmets, body armor, magazines, and backpacks—is all available, along with various items such as first-aid kits, ammo resupplies, binoculars, and vehicles, each of which contributes to experience growth for different roles, such as medic, support, scout, and driver.

On the one hand, even though a combat zone has been designated in the center of the map, for a 100-player match, the experience mostly boils down to “10 minutes of running around and 5 seconds of actual combat.” I often find myself just trailing behind the main group, or when I’m on my own, getting hit by a sniper shot and panicking as I flee.
However, there is one rather counterintuitive fact here: long before the game’s release, Bulkhead had already stated publicly—on more than one occasion—that “the hype would fade.”

On the day of release, Brammer responded on X to discussions about the sustainability of the game’s popularity, displaying a rare dose of “realism”: “War Dog will continue to lose players in the coming months as the hype fades.“This doesn’t mean it’s a bad game—it’s not even a problem; we originally planned for 5,000 concurrent users.”

At the Gamescom 2026 in Cologne, Mark Pinney, CFO and Senior Game Director at Bulkhead, and CEO Joe Brammer were interviewed. When asked if PvE content would be added in future updates, Brammer’s response exceeded expectations: ““We’ve already developed the entire gameplay system—you can even play it right now, though it’s still quite rough around the edges. In fact, our vision is that when you purchase Warhounds and own a Warhounds account, we’ll continue to release DLC over the next few years, and that’s what the new game modes will be.”
Brammer concluded, “We’ll release other modes as DLC to continue funding the game, keep it growing, and ensure players continue to enjoy it.”

Putting the information from the above interviews together, it’s not hard to see Bulkhead’s long-term strategy: sustain the studio with a one-time-purchase game, spend one to two years in early access to polish it thoroughly, and then use subsequent DLCs to introduce new gameplay modes to cater to players who aren’t satisfied with a single mode.

This path is, of course, a difficult one to navigate. Since it doesn’t rely on high DAU, every new model requires convincing players all over again to keep spending; and since it rejects Tencent’s unimaginable budgets, there’s little room for trial and error.“An endless budget” was once seen as a kind of “original sin” for Bulkhead within Tencent’s system at the time, but after breaking away from Tencent, it has become the “freedom” that allows Bulkhead to thrive today.

title: Moss developer Polyarc Games announces closure
event_sentences: Moss developer Polyarc Games is shutting down after 12 years in operation.
GamesIndustry.biz has reached out to Polyarc for further context on the decision to shut the studio.
Polyarc's closure follows the launch of Moss: The Forgotten Relic two months ago, which brought together the original two games outside of VR.
Earlier this year, Polyarc laid off 30 employees after it was unable to secure funding following the cancellation of a major project.

The studio released its debut VR adventure puzzle game Moss in 2018, followed by a sequel in 2022. Last year saw the launch of its online competitive VR strategy game, Glassbreakers: Champions of Moss.
Polyarc raised $3.5 million in 2016 to develop Moss and secured an additional $9 million in 2020 to expand into augmented reality.

Speaking to GamesIndustry.biz in 2021 , Polyarc's publishing and communications director Lincoln Davis said AR was something the developer was "heavily looking into" to "evolve as a studio and adapt as a market changes."

"When we came on with PlayStation with Moss, it was so early on in what type of content it was and it was a complete game experience... So if we can be early on with other technical advances and be that pioneer but add that Polyarc flavour or that Polyarc level of polish too, that would be great for us as a studio."

title: New StarCraft title to launch in 2030, will be an open-world FPS
event_sentences: Blizzard Entertainment has announced that the next StarCraft title will shift from real-time strategy to an open-world first-person shooter.
Revealed at BlizzCon 2026 , the third installment in the franchise, titled StarCraft, is scheduled for release in 2030. Blizzard general manager and vice president Dan Hay leads the project.

In an interview with IGN , Hay explained the team's decision to pursue an open-world format: "For us, when we think about the themes and we think about the opportunity for you to be on the battlefield and for you to go out and think about the vista, the opportunity to explore, and then to discover, and then to disrupt."
StarCraft's 2030 release will be the franchise's first new title since StarCraft 2: Legacy of the Void, which launched in 2015. The original StarCraft debuted in 1998.

Blizzard has previously attempted to develop a StarCraft FPS twice. The first, StarCraft Ghost, was announced in 2002 but cancelled in 2006 after delays. Another project, codenamed Ares, was cancelled in 2019 to prioritise Diablo 4 and Overwatch 2 .
Of course, StarCraft was not the only major announcement from this year's BlizzCon.
Diablo 5 was announced for spring 2029, along with new content for Diablo 4. Netflix is also developing an animated Diablo series.

Blizzard also announced World of Warcraft: Forever, a remastered and expanded version of the original game featuring three new zones, over 1,000 new quests, nine dungeons, two raids, and the new Skyborne race.
World of Warcraft: Forever's beta begins September 17, with the full release scheduled for November 4.

title: "What's the harm in asking?" – Dlala Studios on taking a big swing to get comedy legend Bob Mortimer for the upcoming game Murals
event_sentences: He's one of the country's top comedians, having starred in the double act Reeves and Mortimer, and he recently won the UK version of Amazon's Last One Laughing game show. He's also – as revealed at Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026 – a voice performer in the upcoming game Murals from developer Dlala Studios.
Aj Grand-Scrutton | Image credit: Dlala Studios

"One day I was sitting at my desk, and thought: 'What's the harm in just asking?'," Grand-Scrutton tells GamesIndustry.biz at Gamescom. "So I rung up Mark [Landers] at Side , and I just said, 'Hey dude, is there any chance we could reach out to Bob Mortimer's people?' And he went, 'Oh yeah, hold on Aj mate, I'll get back to you'. And in a couple of hours he called me back, and he was like, we've found his agent and manager, they like the idea, they're interested. Bob wants to see a script."

All they had was a "bunch of gags" at that point, so Grand-Scrutton and Abbott stayed up all night writing a two-to-three-page script, then waited for Bob's verdict. The Dlala founder says it was "the longest 48 hours" of his life.
Murals features Bob Mortimer as 'Magic Dave' | Image credit: Dlala Studios
Later down the line, Grand-Scrutton was in London for a recording session with Mortimer – Dlala always directs its voiceover work.

"I'm not going to say we directed him, because he didn't need it: Everything that came out of his mouth was perfect," the studio founder laughs. "Honestly, the Bob Mortimer you see on television, he's even a hundred times nicer and funnier than that in person."

Securing a celebrity of Mortimer's calibre is a far cry from Dlala's rather humble roots. Founded in 2012 by Grand-Scrutton and Craig Thomas – who had met at Jagex – the outfit initially operated out of Grand-Scrutton's garage in Witham, Essex. Now the company is 43 staff strong and is based in an office around the corner from where Grand-Scrutton grew up.
Dlala made the 2020 game Battletoads | Image credit: Dlala Studios/Xbox Game Studios/Rare

Since those early days, the studio has made a name for itself working on other companies' IP. In 2020, the company released Battletoads, based on the iconic Rare franchise, before launching Disney Illusion Island three years later .

The Battletoads deal came about after a period where Dlala was doing work-for-hire; one project the company was working on was Sea of Thieves. A combination of earned trust and persistence helped the studio land the IP.

"With Battletoads, Microsoft let Rare have a lot of autonomy with that IP back in the day," Grand-Scrutton explains. "We helped out on Sea of Thieves. Dlala was about 12 people at the time, and for the six months before Sea of Thieves came out, the whole of Dlala was helping Rare get that finished. And I think that earned trust.
Sony emphasises its relationship with Kojima Productions "remains strong" and "looks forward to continued close collaboration" with the developer

"I met [former Rare studio head] Craig Duncan in the year we formed, 2012, and every year, I sent him multiple pitches for Battletoads, trying to wear him down. It wasn't until 2016 that he said we should do this, and we still didn't get it over the line until 2018. That was a real kismet of stuff; we proved ourselves with Sea of Thieves and Game Pass needed portfolio pieces. And once that came out, it showed the quality of what we could do and deliver end to end."
Disney's Illusion Island came out in 2023 | Image credit: Dlala Studios/Disney

That, in turn, led to a deal with Disney for Illusion Island – which marked Dlala's second deal with the firm, after an initial project didn't work out. "I did a rather honest GI.biz interview that I shouldn't have done, where I mentioned we had a Disney game in 2015 that got cancelled in 2016, and I thought we'd never work with them ever again," recalls Grand-Scrutton.

"After Battletoads came out, we were looking at what we could do next, and I said as a joke: 'Oh, why don't we give Disney a call?' and we all went 'Oh ha ha'. Then we all went: 'Oh, why don't we give Disney a call?' So we spoke. It was kind of like high school boyfriend and girlfriend meeting up after 20 years: this is how I've changed, this is how you've changed. And we said on that call: 'Should we give it another go? Should we try and do a game together?'"

After securing those IP deals with Rare and Disney, you'd think that Dlala's next move might be another licensed property. But instead the studio has made a bet on making its own IP. "We were presented with a real opportunity where we had a little bit of money ourselves in the bank so we could afford to pay for half of the development," the Dlala boss explains. "We found a wonderful family office in Canada that was looking to invest in something. And we'd learned a lot working with Disney. We worked on Illusion Island for, it was like five years including the DLC we had people on that project, and we loved it. It's literally a highlight of my entire life."
Grant Allen | Image credit: Dlala Studios

"We kind of just said, why don't we take all these learnings, all this stuff we've done, all these tools we've made over the last decade, and do something that Dlala owns? This is our IP, this is something we can publish. We can't blame anyone for the failure if we're perfectly in charge. And we decided to just take the jump and gamble on it."

Murals is a combat game, explains design director Grant Allen, "but it's a combat game where it's easy to pick up, easy to play, but has depth to it. And on top of that, we took a lot of inspiration from rogue-likes [in terms of items] for augmenting that combat. But in our game, because it's linear, they're persistent. So you build up this huge catalogue of what we call Eeries, which you're able to switch in and out." He describes these trinkets as being like a chemistry set, where different Eeries can add different attributes to weapons. And of course, there's Magic Dave, Bob Mortimer's character, who's in charge of the Vending Machine of Delights.
Murals sees Dlala Studios striking out solo | Image credit: Dlala Studios

"We've always been quite a sensible studio in the sense that you will never ever find royalties in our finance spreadsheets in terms of projections," he says. "As far as we're concerned, our games will make zero, because I'm not going to bet people's jobs on the success of the title that I'm in charge of. We have bet the house on this original, but we've secured the team outside of it, so there's no risk to the team if this game doesn't do well, except for we'd all be devastated. So we're putting everything into this. We have sunk every penny into making this game the best it could possibly be."

Dlala has opted to self-publish Murals, and has hired Marcus Purvis, head of publishing, to handle this side of the business. Purvis is no stranger to the studio, having previously met Grand-Scrutton and co when they were part of Microsoft's Lift London incubator program.
Marcus Purvis | Image credit: Dlala Studios

"Last year, Aj was talking to me about the game and showing me," Purvis says. "It looked incredible. He was saying the opportunity is there and we want to publish this and can I be a part of that? It's a no-brainer. We're doing it ourselves, and we're learning along the way. The beauty of doing it ourselves is that we can make decisions very quickly, and we love to do that.

One example of the freedom and agility self-publishing affords is the decision to do a limited-edition comic book that ties into Murals. "We met someone who made comic books," explains Grand-Scrutton. "We had a conversation, and about nine weeks later we'd written it, started the art, and then suddenly we had a comic book," he says. "We can't really do that if someone else is in charge of the budget.

"And something like the comic, there's no return on investment. And I think that is the thing that we get [from] self-publishing over working with publisher, is that publishers have to be driven by how successful the game's going to be. And a lot of that is the ROI, what's going to come back. For us, we've got focus… We've got amazing partners in China, and Marcus is making sure we're ticking all the boxes to make the money. But then we go, 'Should we waste a few grand and do something really cool, like making a comic book?'"

In many ways, despite lacking a license, Murals is a continuation of what Dlala is best at. "What we're really known for, I think, is how we combine our gameplay with our aesthetics," says Grand-Scrutton, noting the studio's focus on hand-drawn art and combat. "And then it's our humour, whether you find it funny or not."

title: Roblox creators will soon be able to publish games on multiple platforms as standalone apps
event_sentences: Roblox will enable creators to publish their games on mobile, PC, and console through the Roblox Everywhere initiative.

Announced at this year's Roblox Developers Conference , the company said creators will be able to make their games available as standalone apps on multiple platforms, with Roblox "powering the technology and services underneath."

It's not yet confirmed if standalone apps will be available on third-party storefronts. A Roblox representative told PC Gamer that it "will start with a select set of gaming developers and storefronts to test, and will share more details soon."

By the end of 2026, players will be able to join games directly in-browser from the Experience Details page, without needing an app or installation. This feature will launch on Chrome first, with additional browsers to follow.
Roblox also announced that creators will be able to enable offline solo play. This feature will enter early access before its full release by mid-2027.
Additionally, Roblox's engine will receive updates including an orthographic camera, animated image containers, direct sprite-sheet imports, and enhanced UI features and gradients.

An "AI creation layer" will be added to Roblox's cloud operating system "built for the complexity of games." The mobile, AI-powered Build feature will expand to Serbia and Singapore after its alpha launch in New Zealand.
Earlier this year, Roblox introduced agentic AI tools that allow creators to "build a game with a single prompt."

Roblox also announced Roblox Wallet and Roblox Card to provide "creators faster, more flexible access to their earnings." These features will allow creators to receive daily payments in their local currency and transfer funds to other Roblox or external bank accounts.

Roblox Wallet will be rolled out this December to independent creators 18 or older in the US, with plans to expand internationally next year. Roblox will also produce a physical card in 2027 for creators "to spend their available balance directly, anywhere it's accepted."
In its latest financial results , Roblox reported a 36% increase in revenue to $1.5 billion.
Despite higher bookings, the company faced a shortfall due to reduced per-hour monetisation among younger users in the US and Canada. As a result, Roblox shares declined by 70% .

"This underlying mix shift was compounded by changes in our recommendation algorithm, which optimises for long-term retention and is, therefore, providing more impressions for highly retentive games at the expense of near-term monetisation," said chief financial officer Naveen Chopra. "And in Q2, the bookings impact of this trade-off on younger users was greater than we anticipated."

Chopra told investors that while the company expects to "mitigate the monetisation headwind" by improving its algorithms with age-check data for better recommendations, "monetisation weakness is likely to continue."

title: Roblox plans to let creators turn their games into standalone apps
event_sentences: Roblox has unveiled a raft of new features at its developer conference, including plans that could see Roblox experiences ship as standalone apps outside the main Roblox client.

Under the banner Roblox Everywhere, creators will soon be able to package their games as independent apps for mobile, PC and console, with Roblox handling the backend. Roblox has not given a timeline for when the first standalone experiences might arrive, or detailed exactly how or where they’ll be distributed.
Offline play is coming too. Creators will be able to build a solo mode alongside multiplayer in the same game, though it won’t be fully available until mid-2027 and after an early access period.

2D and puzzle games are getting dedicated support for the first time through new engine features and UI upgrades. Turn-based, asynchronous multiplayer games are getting a new notification system and will be tested in Studio Beta in October ahead of a full release before the end of the year.

Roblox is also introducing Roblox Wallet, a financial account with a third-party partner that pays creator earnings out daily in real currency. It’s expected to roll out in the US later this year, with a companion Roblox Card letting creators spend that balance directly. Wallet is expected to expand to other countries next year, with Roblox Card following in 2027.

There’s more for Build users, too. Build, the prompt-based game creation tool, is taking its trial run beyond New Zealand and into Serbia and Singapore. Creators using Build will get more control over their projects, with a new asset library and the ability to build from desktop among the additions. They can already review performance data and set up monetisation, and will soon be able to launch ads from their phones too. Roblox puts the number of games published through Build at close to 9,000 so far, and says the majority of those creators, 71%, had never used Roblox Studio before.

Furthermore, later this year, a new Scene Generator tool will let creators turn a prompt and reference image into a ready-made layout in Build or Studio, which they can then refine and develop further in Studio.

Roblox is also testing a new ranking metric based on the number of first-time players a game pulls onto the platform, rather than just short-term engagement. Roblox creators have made more than $5bn through DevEx since its 2013 launch, with around $1.7 n of that earned in the past year alone, said the UGC firm.

title: Blizzard Explains Why The StarCraft Shooter Coming In 2030 Was Announced Now
event_sentences: Thanks to rumors and reports, the announcement of a new StarCraft game taking the form of an open-world shooter did not come as a complete surprise at BlizzCon's Opening Ceremony . What is surprising is when it's coming: 2030. That's a long time from now, and we've heard other developers lament announcing their games too soon . So what made Blizzard reveal StarCraft so far in advance?
Hay said that with Blizzard being confident in what it's developed so far, it didn't want to further delay going public and getting the benefit of putting it in front of fans.
Still, Hay said he sees value in attaching a date to the project and having developers examine their decision making through that target.

"Yeah, we also know that the date of 2030 is one of those things where--I like a date," Hay said. "I like the idea that there's something out there for us to go after. It helps us sometimes when you get into a meeting and you're thinking about the creative, and you go, 'All right, well how long are we going to wax poetic on this? How long are we going to think about this?' The answer is, 'Can we get all this done by that date?' If the answer is no: Let's rethink, let's refocus, and let's make sure we're thinking about players wanting to get this at the highest level of fidelity possible, but in a reasonable amount of time. That's why we picked that date."

"I think our focus is we're building a new team. We've got a whole bunch of energy to it from the standpoint of this really comes from what we call a creative ache, right?" Hay said. "We really started with--when you think about the genesis of it--what's the story we want to tell? How do we want to make this game unique and different? The answer is, in previous versions of StarCraft, you were up above, looking down at the battlefield, and you had the deployment of many Marines and many different factions. This time, we were like, 'What if it was just one? What if you only got one suit? What if you had to take care of it?'

"We use the analogy of: You know that first time you get your first car? The first car was probably not great, but it was amazing because it was your first car. What happens when you get this thing and you have to take care of it? What happens when you start to see a world that has opportunity and discovery, but things that you can also pick up and maybe make your armor better? How do you go out into the world and start to take care of this thing and push against it?

"Then you start to think about, 'Wait a minute, I'm in this armor.' You saw it in the teaser: The character in the teaser gets the armor and is feeling super powerful and everything, and it's a 10-foot-tall thing that weighs a thousand pounds. You think, 'There's nothing that I can't beat.' Then you watch his face as the doors open, and you hear that growl of the Zerg. You watch his face--and we spent a ton of time just on the facial expression--of just loss, just the understanding of the distance between what we believe we can do and the reality of what life teaches us. We captured all that in that moment on his face of, 'I might be in trouble here.' But he put up a valiant effort.

title: StarCraft Reboot Is “Focusing On Single-Player,” Creative Director Says
event_sentences: StarCraft is "focusing on single-player," StarCraft creative director and general manager Dan Hay and associate manager of development operations Anna Lee Hertling said in an interview with GameSpot.

One of the biggest announcements of BlizzCon 2026 was the return of StarCraft, described as an open-world shooter and slated for a 2030 release. Aside from its impressive reveal cinematic, there wasn't much additional information about how StarCraft would play or what the shooter reboot of the RTS franchise would entail.
Now, we have some more details. When asked whether StarCraft would be single-player or co-op, Hay said the team is "focusing on single player."

"We are focused right now on the conversation of focusing on single-player, focusing on that Marine fantasy, and then making sure that we think about what it is to be that character," Hay said. "That's what we're saying for now."

He said players will play as a named character that can "build a reputation and a rapport" with other in-game characters. He said the game's story will have a beginning, middle, and an "end," and that Blizzard wants it to feel like a "boxed product." Thought it's story will have an end, Hay said Blizzard wants the game to be one players can visit, explore, leave, and come back to.

"We like a named character, right?" Hay said. "When it comes down to this, we want to be able to make sure that what you have is a character that has a name, a character that people in the world can know. What it does it it makes the story have a little bit more life to it."
Other tidbits shared by Hay during the interview include the fact that StarCraft will be third-person rather than first, as well as why Blizzard decided to announce it now , four years in advance.

title: The StarCraft Shooter Is A Third-Person Game, And Blizzard Insists That You Have To Feel “Powerful”
event_sentences: If you walked away from the StarCraft reveal excited for the franchise to return, but unsure what this new game even is, you're not alone. Aside from being described during the BlizzCon Opening Ceremony as an open-world shooter, Blizzard didn't share much else. In an interview with GameSpot, Blizzard GM Dan Hay provided a few more details, including the fact that it's a third-person game.

"Oh, that's easy," Hay said when GameSpot asked him about whether StarCraft will be a first- or third-person game. "I want to be able to see my armor. First thing we did is we built it, put it on a turntable, and spun it around like, 'Ah, awesome, cool!' I want to be able to see it, so third-person, right?

Hay spoke to us a great deal about the fantasy of having this armor to protect you. Asked about character progression or customization, he said, "If I was to get—in theory, hypothetically, purely hypothetically—this is what I would want: I would want to be able to make sure that my armor can be made better, stronger, and different. I would also want to be able to make sure that I could make it feel like mine. I would want it to be a visitation of the legacy of the things that I had done. I would want to show that it looked different from the first moment that I got it to the last moment I got it. So, read into that how much you will hypothetically, but that's what I would want as a player."

title: You’ll Fight The Protoss In StarCraft, Too, Don’t Worry
event_sentences: StarCraft's reveal trailer squarely put the focus on the Terrans, who later in the cinematic face a terrifying confrontation with the Zerg. The franchise's three franchises--including the Protoss--have always been a central element of what distinguishes StarCraft from other strategy games. Although the Protoss were effectively absent from the trailer, they are a foe you will face at some point.

"The answer to that question is I absolutely unequivocally can't say," Hay said. "But what I can do is tell you what I would want as a player. I'll hint at sort of not what we're doing, but some of the things that we think about.
Hay did point out something that was easy to miss in the trailer: a small hint of the Protoss.

"You saw more than the Zerg in the trailer," he said. "If you look a little deeper, there's a moment when the thing opens and you hear that great horn go off. If you look in the background—just in the background, adjust the lighting just a tiny bit—you'll see some architecture that is very not Terran and very not Zerg. It's there."

Hay also confirmed a third-person perspective for StarCraft . While the trailer may not reflect gameplay, it does showcase one way that could impact the feel of the game, as we see the Terran soldier look up in terror at the size of a Zerg Overlord, something you ordinarily only see from an isometric camera view in past StarCraft games.
He also said StarCraft will have a "single-player focus" and offered some insight into why the game was announced now despite arriving in 2030 .

title: First GTA 6 Actor Officially Confirmed, And It’s A Big Name
event_sentences: Root, who is known for voicing King of the Hill's Bill Dauterive and playing Milton Waddams in Office Space among hundreds of other credits, will play Brian Heder. Although he didn't confirm as much in the interview clip from AP, Root's distinctive voice makes him easy to pick out from the various GTA 6 trailers.
GTA 6 will be released on November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and Rockstar is hard at work fighting drones and hackers to keep the game's secrets safe.

title: Resident Evil Movie Director Comments On Physical Media Debate
event_sentences: Speaking to IndieWire , Cregger said he is "not a physical media guy" today. He said he was previously, but he is a person who often loses or damages the physical media he owns, and he doesn't have enough space for all the discs and boxes he might collect.
Cregger said he is "not bent out of shape" about downloading games because "at least it means it's always going to be there when I need it."
At the same time, Cregger said he's aware that companies can "just delete it" even after someone has paid. "And, yeah, that's too bad. I don't like that," he said.

Sony's decision to end support for physical games may make sense financially, but it's upsetting people who still buy physical media, and there are many of these people. In the last year, Sony sold many millions of physical game discs . But starting in January 2028, discs from Sony and other companies will no longer be supported, so everyone will have to buy games through the PlayStation Store.

The move to end support physical game discs on PlayStation is really about profitability and control , experts say. Microsoft recently announced a disc-to-digital program for Xbox , but many believe the company's next-gen platform, Project Helix , will not support discs.
The Resident Evil movie, which is backed by Sony Pictures and PlayStation Productions, is set for release on September 18.

title: StarCraft: Release Date, Gameplay, And Everything We Know
event_sentences: Amidst a flurry of rumors and teases, a brand-new StarCraft game was officially revealed at BlizzCon 2026 . While the series started off as a real-time strategy experience, the new StarCraft is switching gears and has been billed as an open-world shooter. While it won't be out for several more years, Blizzard did reveal several details about the game, along with a slick cinematic trailer to set the stage for what's to come. Here's a closer look at everything we know about StarCraft so far.
StarCraft release date

You're going to have to be patient, as Blizzard is targeting a 2030 release date for StarCraft. Why was the game revealed so early? Blizzard general manager Dan Hay said that the company had made enough progress on the game to officially announce it and gather feedback from the reveal. "There’s a moment when you're making a game where you're like, 'Have we landed the emotion? Do we feel like we have enough of the verve, the identity, and the feel of it to start to share it?" Hay said to GameSpot . "About a year ago, we started to feel like we were there, so we were like, ‘Okay, it’s time to show it. It’s time to get feedback.'"

While official platforms have yet to be revealed, it's a safe bet that StarCraft will probably launch for PC. But what consoles could it land on? By 2030, we're expecting to be playing on Sony's PlayStation 6 and Microsoft's Xbox successor, Project Helix , so we might be looking at a next-gen game when StarCraft eventually launches.

Unsurprisingly, StarCraft's only public footage currently is a cinematic trailer. What we do know is that this will be a major departure from the RTS days of StarCraft, as the game will be a third-person experience focusing on single-player and co-op elements. Hay explained that players will be able to build their reputation and rapport with in-game characters as they step into a Marine's power armour. There's also a big focus on the power fantasy of being one of these Dominion soldiers

"Combat has to feel powerful,"  Hay explained . "You're in this armor; you're a living tank. You have to feel powerful. When you hold that Gauss rifle, and the thing weighs something ridiculous, you have to feel like you’re just pushing through the Zerg. The Zerg have to feel like those raptorial claws are going to shuck you like an oyster in that thing. So you have to feel the weight of all that."

Yes and no, by the sound of things. While the focus is primarily on giving players a single-player open-world adventure to enjoy, Hay said that StarCraft's story will have a definitive conclusion, and that Blizzard wants it to feel like a "boxed product" that players can return to whenever they want. "We like a named character, right?" Hay said. "When it comes down to this, we want to be able to make sure that what you have is a character that has a name, a character that people in the world can know. What it does is it makes the story have a little bit more life to it."

Speaking of the story, Blizzard is keeping a tight lid on the narrative. The cinematic trailer hinted at new Dominion recruits being thrown into a meat-grinder against Zerg forces-- and you'll also encounter the Protoss . Hay has confirmed that StarCraft is set 70 years after StarCraft 2: Legacy of the Void--that won't be confusing, a leap forward in time that could allow for some bold storytelling and new characters to emerge.

Even with the Protoss reclaiming Aiur, the reformation of the Dominion under Valerian Mengsk, and Zagara aiming to lead the Zerg into an era of peace, nothing is ever certain in the StarCraft galaxy and it's going to be interesting to learn what happened in those decades.

title: Release The Resident Evil: Whitest Kids ‘U Know Cut
event_sentences: The Resident Evil movie from Barbarian and Weapons director Zach Cregger releases on September 18, and now he's revealed a key detail about what people won't experience in the movie. Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter , Cregger shared what he learned from test screenings, and that was that an earlier version had too much humor.

"I learned [from test screenings] that people really liked the movie, but they thought it was too funny. So over the course of my testing, I stripped out as much of the jokes as possible,” Cregger said. “I then found that not only did the audience enjoy the movie more, but I also liked the movie a lot more. A little bit of humor goes a long way in a horror movie, and there’s not a single joke I took out of this movie that I miss.”

Also in the interview, Cregger discussed how he understands he cannot please everyone, especially a group as passionate as gamers. He previously said he felt like his press tour was more of an "apology tour" because he's not delivering the movie some fans wanted. However, speaking to The Hollywood Reporter, Cregger said he is not interested in pleasing everyone; instead, his North Star is making the kind of Resident Evil movie he wants to make.

"If I tried to please everybody, I’d end up pleasing nobody. That much is obvious,” Cregger said. “I just have to be okay with people voicing their opinion. I’m a grown-up. When I took this on, I understood what I was walking into. So it would be weird for me to act surprised or bent out of shape that the thing that was obviously going to happen is now happening.”

He went on to say there are fans of the games who "specifically love the lore and the characters and the nitty-gritty details of the backstory." But Cregger's movie tells a different story, involving no characters from the games.

"I’m not putting any of the legacy characters into this movie. So if that is what you love about these games, then you’re going to feel a certain way about it. ' Here comes yet another Hollywood movie, and they’re once again not doing Leon and all the characters I was hoping they were going to do ,'" he said.

The Resident Evil movie releases on September 18, with screenings starting a night earlier. The film is expected to be a huge hit, potentially achieving the biggest opening weekend in franchise history .

title: Resident Evil Movies Were On Ice Until Zach Cregger Came Along
event_sentences: On paper, Zach Cregger directing a Resident Evil movie sounds like a smart move. The director has earned critical acclaim for his work on spooky flicks like Barbarian and Weapons, while Resident Evil is experiencing a resurgence thanks to several years of hit games. But that's a pairing that almost never came to be, as after the dismal box office performance of 2021's Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City, movie distributor Constantin Films--who own the film rights to Resident Evil-- wanted to give the franchise a chance to rest before greenlighting a new project.

That all changed when Cregger approached the company, as Constantin Films CEO Oliver Berben said that he already had ideas in mind for the Resident Evil movie he wanted to make. This was prior to the release of Weapons, as Barbarian had shown that the former member of the comedy troupe The Whitest Kids U Know was a heck of a horror movie director; his follow-up film put him on the Hollywood map as a rising star behind the camera.

"Zach Cregger actually approached us, together with Roy Lee (a producer on Cregger's movies). He basically came to us,  and asked if this franchise, if this IP, was available," Berben said in an episode of The Town. "And it was really strange because at that time, first of all, we were in that situation that we said, 'Okay, we're going to leave it alone. We're going to need to find a completely new way on how to adapt this for the future.'  And on the other hand, Zach, just only came out of Barbarian.  So it wasn't at all that everybody was jumping on it immediately."

Berben added that Cregger had not seen the live-action movies directed by Paul W.S. Anderson, and that Cregger's pitch of a "normal guy" thrown into a nightmarish situation won over the studio's leadership.  It's not too long to go now before Resident Evil hits theaters--September 18--and ahead of its release, Cregger has been doing the media rounds to talk about the movie. The director recently spoke about how Resident Evil was originally a funnier movie before he dialed back the jokes, and he even took time to weigh in on the physical media debate for video games --spoiler: he's fine with digital games, even if he's aware of potential pitfalls with them.

If box office predictions are on the money, Resident Evil could scare up the best opening weekend  in the entire film franchise, as analysts are estimating that it could make between $40 and $50 million in North American alone.

title: Diablo 5 Will Have The Most Classes Of Any Game In The Series
event_sentences: Diablo 5 will launch with more classes than any other game in the franchise, according to game director Joe Shely.

Shely revealed more details about what to expect from Diablo 5's launch roster during a BlizzCon 2026 panel, following the game's surprise reveal (and Spring 2029 release window) as part of BlizzCon's opening ceremony . During the panel, Blizzard revealed three of Diablo 5's classes : Monk, Demon Hunter, and the new Plague Knight.
"Diablo 5 is going to launch with more classes than ever before," Shely said. "And I don't just mean more classes than another Diablo game at ship. I mean more classes total."
That means Blizzard is aiming for nine or 10 classes in Diablo 5 at launch, depending on whether or not they are counting Diablo 4's newly revealed Amazon class .

"What that does...it allows us to, if you started playing Diablo in Diablo 3, you probably know the Demon Hunter, and you can jump into Diablo 5 and have an experience that's familiar and new at the same time," Shely said. "It's a new representation of the class. It's going to be different, but you're still going to have twin crossbows. We're going to pay off that nostalgia you have and that feeling of what that experience was like. Having a lot of classes lets us do that in a way we haven't been able to do before. It also affords us the opportunity to explore new classes like the Plague Knight."

With work on Diablo 5 in full swing, Blizzard confirmed Diablo 4 won't receive new expansions going forward. It will, however, continue to receive new seasonal content. Season of Hell's Legacy goes live September 15 and sees the return of Deckard Cain. The iconic Horadrim from previous Diablo games will task players with taking on echoes of the Prime Evils, including Diablo himself.

title: Lies Of P’s Wizard Of Oz Tease May Have Just Gotten A Lot More Interesting
event_sentences: Lies of P was a big hit when it was first released, and several years after it was confirmed that a sequel was in development , a new trademark by developer Neowiz has popped up online. As spotted on the European Union Intellectual Property Office website (via ThePhraseMaker ), the studio has registered a trademark for " Wonders of O ," suggesting that the game will put own macabre spin on L. Frank Baum's The Wonderful Wizard of Oz books.

The listing is for "interactive multimedia software for playing games," but beyond that, no other details on the game can be gleaned from the registration. Lies of P had previously hinted at a trip to the Emerald City; in the mid-credits sequence, a familiar pair of ruby-red shoes could be seen. Neowiz will have free rein to put a souls-like twist on the book--which entered the public domain in 1956--since the original story includes all manner of fantastical creatures. From flying monkeys to the Tin Man, the Wicked Witch of the East and the manipulative Wizard of Oz himself, there's plenty to work with here--and we've got a few ideas of our own for where Agent P can travel to next.

Following the launch of the game in 2023, Neowiz continued its twisted rendition of Pinocchio with the Overture expansion in 2025. A prequel, the expansion shed light on the events that led to the Puppet Frenzy massacre and subsequent collapse of the city of Krat.  The game also came to Switch 2  earlier this year.

Neowiz has periodically spoken about its approach to crafting a Lies of P sequel, and in January, the developer said it was exploring how technology-based solutions , like AI, could be used to "automate routine operational tasks" during game development.

While the use of generative AI in games is a controversial topic in the West, in countries like South Korea it's actively used and considered an essential set of tools. "By processing data faster, our teams will arrive at better, more informed strategic decisions on how best to support our developers and engage with our community," Neowiz co-CEO Sean Kim said.

title: Red Dead 2 Actor Shares A Gross Secret About The Game
event_sentences: Actor Roger Clark played Arthur Morgan in Rockstar's celebrated 2018 Western Red Dead Redemption 2, and his performance was memorable for many reasons. In the game, Arthur suffers from tuberculosis, and he coughs a lot as a result. Was it challenging for Clark to perform those sequences in particular? Yes, but it was "not as bad as you'd think," Clark said in a recent interview, in part because sometimes Clark recorded when he himself had a bad cough.

Clark told Cade Onder that he had "five years to spread it out," regarding his voice-capture performance in Red Dead 2, and that's part of the reason why it wasn't as difficult as you might imagine. Additionally, Clark said if he was performing a "really bad coughing scene," this would be saved for the end of a given recording day, when his voice was already hoarse from all the work.
Beyond this, Clark said over that five-year period, when he recorded his lines, he, like most people, got sick--and he used this to his benefit.

"In five years, there's plenty of colds. There was a lot of data we got that was pretty damn genuine. […] I'd be like 'Hey, I've got a cold, let me get in there.' And they'd be like, 'Okay.' […] Nice good bit of phlegm," he said.

With more than 87 million copies sold, Red Dead 2 is one of the top five best-selling games of all time . Rockstar's next big release is GTA 6 , which launches in November for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

title: The Last Of Us 2 Multiplayer Mod Canceled “On Behalf Of Sony,” Dev Says
event_sentences: Naughty Dog's The Last of Us franchise featured a multiplayer mode in Factions, and while the studio planned to add multiplayer to the sequel, it abandoned those ambitions before release. A modder spent months this year working on a multiplayer mod for The Last of Us 2, but its lead has now said it's not going to be released due to a request from Sony to shut it down.

Modder @Speclizer_ said on social media that the mod was due to launch this month. However, they said they "recently received a letter on behalf of Sony Interactive Entertainment requesting for the mod not to be released."

Speclizer said this is an "extremely sad" development, but they hope people who supported the project will stick with them for the next one. Their next project will be "something of my own" as opposed to an extension of an existing game.
"Thank you all for the incredible amount of support over the last year. I hope to bring you something bigger and better soon!" Speclizer said.
GameSpot has contacted Sony in an attempt to get more details.

Naughty Dog was set to expand The Last of Us into an online multiplayer experience in a very big way with The Last of Us Online. The game was in development for years with significant resources dedicated to it, and it was reportedly almost ready for release . However, in December 2023, Naughty Dog canceled the game , saying at the time that it was going to focus on single-player games instead.

Also at that time, Naughty Dog confirmed that it had two single-player games in development. One has been revealed to be Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, while the other remains a mystery; many believe it's The Last of Us 3 .

In other Naughty Dog-related news, studio head Neil Druckmann has confirmed that the studio has no creative involvement in the upcoming third season of HBO's The Last of Us . This is a big change, as Druckmann himself was personally and directly involved in the previous two seasons.

title: 报道称PlayStation因预算与延期问题放弃《Physint》
event_sentences: 据彭博社最新报道，索尼之所以放弃与《潜龙谍影》创作者小岛秀夫合作开发PlayStation新作《Physint》，主要原因包括项目多次错过开发节点，以及预算超支风险。
正如IGN此前采访的分析师所指出的那样，在经历多款第一方游戏失败或取消之后，索尼似乎正在收紧游戏开发支出，并对制作过程中的开发里程碑执行更加严格的要求。
此前，索尼已经在生命周期极短的《星鸣特攻》、Naughty Dog最终取消的《最后生还者 Online》，以及目前表现依然不佳的《失落星船：马拉松》等项目上投入数亿美元。
报道称，《死亡搁浅》及其续作的营收表现，也是索尼作出决定的因素之一。
Alinea Analytics此前的分析显示，《死亡搁浅2》的销量目前已经放缓至较低水平，游戏此前多次进行明显降价促销，但都没有显著刺激销量，其营收也仍然远低于前作。
另外，虽然从PS1时代开始，小岛秀夫就与PlayStation保持着长期合作关系，但过去与这位《潜龙谍影》创作者共事过的不少索尼高层，如今已经离开公司或不再担任原来的职位。

title: Rockstar为防止泄露采取了极为严格的措施
event_sentences: 这场听证会将决定去年被解雇的31名《GTA6》开发人员后续命运，而在相关文件中，Rockstar也首次详细披露了公司为了防止安全泄露，究竟采取了多么严格的措施。
此前Rockstar正式宣布《GTA6》延期6个月、改至2026年11月19日发售后，Take-Two市值就在一天内蒸发了37.5亿美元。
2025年4月，Rockstar解雇了英国林肯工作室的一名员工，理由是该员工涉嫌向第三方透露《GTA6》的机密信息，而这些信息随后被发布到社交媒体。
Rockstar还提到，2025年两名员工发布的两条看似毫无问题的推文，曾引发一个错误的粉丝理论：有人认为Rockstar会在2025年12月27日发布新的《GTA6》预告，作为游戏正式销售前的预热。
据称，工会目前提出的诉求包括提高薪资透明度、保护员工免受游戏发售后的裁员影响、结束「Crunch」高强度加班文化，以及改善弹性工作安排。

title: Insomniac回应金刚狼气味轨迹争议
event_sentences: 部分玩家希望开发商Insomniac Games加入关闭选项，不过官方表示，这一效果并不会在游戏中一直显示。
这项机制其实早在今年夏季便已公开，但随着本周游戏评测陆续上线，相关讨论再次升温。
他还指出，即使关闭部分辅助和导航选项，这些气味轨迹仍然存在。
部分玩家一度认为，该效果可以通过无障碍设置关闭。
《漫威金刚狼》的官方无障碍功能中确实包含「追逐辅助」选项，可以在追逐环节降低目标的移动速度，但这一功能并不会关闭气味轨迹。
因此，一些玩家认为气味轨迹在游戏中会始终开启，并呼吁Insomniac加入关闭功能。
不过，即便如此，仍有玩家希望游戏能够彻底关闭这种被戏称为「屁气」的视觉提示。

title: 《雷顿教授》开发商回应游戏使用生成式AI
event_sentences: 在粉丝发现《雷顿教授与不可思议的小镇 重制版》《DECAPOLICE》等游戏的宣传片中存在「AI垃圾」后，开发商Level-5就使用生成式AI一事道歉并作出解释。
相关担忧出现在本周早些时候Level-5举行的一场类似任天堂直面会的发布会之后。
这场名为「Level5 Vision 2026 II: Dreams」的发布会首次展示了多款即将推出的游戏，同时也出现了多处被粉丝怀疑使用生成式AI的内容。
观看这场50分钟发布会的观众，花在讨论疑似使用AI证据上的时间，甚至比讨论游戏本身还多，其中涉及《雷顿教授》重制版、《妖怪手表2 霸道》和《DECAPOLICE》等作品。
引发争议的画面大多只出现在背景场景中，但真正让事情演变成这家日本工作室全面争议的，是粉丝不得不首先去质疑Level-5是否使用了AI这件事本身。
但看到他们在这么多游戏里如此明目张胆地使用生成式AI……对，这真的不行。
我们不想要这种AI垃圾。
Level-5社长兼CEO日野晃博也通过X回应争议。
此前他还以自己的动画形象主持了这场发布会。
他发布的内容既是一份道歉，也是一番解释，并确认Level-5确实在部分开发环节中使用了生成式AI。
日野晃博将Level-5大量使用AI形容为「对最新技术的实验」，并补充表示，团队「对于任何因此感到不适的人，诚挚致歉」。
我们主要利用AI来提高将人工创作素材数字化的效率，例如把原画准确转换成3D多边形模型。
大家可以放心，我们推出的游戏中不存在单纯由AI生成的内容。

他表示：「通过AI提高效率节省下来的时间，让我们的创作者能够把更多精力投入到真正的创作本质之中。

title: I've got a soft spot for cozy games with flying in them and these are my 4 favorites
event_sentences: There are as many definitions of "cozy game" as there are cozy gamers, but freedom is a really common element. There's freedom to build in life sims or freedom from time constraints in puzzle games. What is flying but complete and total freedom of exploration?

In the years since Breath of the Wild we've been spoiled for open world games with gliders, but a game with proper flying is even better. In Promise Mascot Agency I can hit my kei truck's boost thruster, nudge its nose up to gain altitude, and bank into a turn for a second pass over the rural sprawl below. It's the most open an open world can be and the freest I ever feel exploring one.

Once you upgrade your kei truck with wings you are unstoppable. This thing is meant to be bashed and crashed into every obstacle you find, which is extra true once you can launch it off a switchback mountain road into an elegant nose dive directly onto a collectible you were looking for. Pure joy.
Also by the studio who made Journey, it has similar flight controls and distance upgrades, but it's a miniature MMO with tons of puzzles and exploration that I love going back to every few months.
Technically, this one is gliding because I don't think you can gain altitude, but exploring the gorgeous lofi island in search of secret areas is exactly what makes flight so fun.

title: After more than 400 hours of Valheim in early access, I love the journey from naked adventurer to godly Viking now more than ever
event_sentences: I'm back on my bullshit, and by bullshit I mean sinking another delightful 100 hours into Valheim —the Viking-themed survival crafting game that sits among my top five most-played games on Steam. With the launch of 1.0 and its new biome, the Deep North, now is the best time to round up your friends and return to ye olde old sea fortresses and swampy castles. A lot has changed in Odin's purgatory.

Perhaps some of that is thanks to skipping last year's Call to Arms update—the patch where Iron Gate dramatically reworked the buffs received from slaying Valheim's giant gods—but now I'm glad I waited. As my total Valheim playtime rapidly approaches the 500-hour mark, I can't help but be impressed by how good a handful of small changes and new items make progression to the endgame feel.

(Image credit: Iron Gate Studios) I've already made biome-specific building collections for every zone too, and even have pared-down versions for quick access in emergencies. We're all guilty of picking fights with Fulings that we can't handle, but I like to pull the ol' Fortnite on 'em. That's code for building a box around myself and crying for help, by the way. Is that not how Fortnite works?

(Image credit: Iron Gate Studios) The boss reworks from last year pair especially well with the breadcrumb directions added in 1.0's cutscenes, too. I won't spoil the whole thing for you, but historically, Valheim didn't do the best job of teaching its Vikings how to play. And I mean, it still doesn't deliver its secrets on a silver platter, but that's more fun when you've got a vague hint about where to go next and a series of boss buffs that all feel viable. Back in my day, we had seven boss buffs, and only one (or maybe two) of them felt viable.

title: My favourite soundtrack of 2026 so far is tucked in one of this year's biggest sleeper hits
event_sentences: I have not been able to stop thinking about Big Walk since I finished the game alongside six of my friends last month. What I had anticipated to be a relatively okay, quick-dirty-fun co-op game unfurled itself into one of the most thoughtful videogames I've ever played, and easily my favourite of 2026 so far. I cannot even begin to explain what a fantastic job developer House House has done at creating an incredibly special, unreplicatable experience that has had me and my pals continuing to talk about it in the weeks since we rolled credits.

(Image credit: Panic) But in the little pockets of the world where it reveals itself, having it cut through the silence makes the moments you spend with it feel even more special. Spread across almost 30 tracks, Australian duo aksfx play around with these delightfully ethereal, pulsing beats and jumping vocals that sound like they should be mildly unsettling on paper, but the execution leads to this delightful feeling of exploration and airiness.

Not only are they moments of respite to bask in for a bit, but they're the perfect backdrop to punctuate cute moments with your pals. Coming across a radio station right as the sun is rising and taking a second to watch it happen as the notes delicately echo around you feels like something straight out of a slice-of-life anime's penultimate episode, the one that makes you bawl your eyes out.

There are so many reasons to love Big Walk, and its music is certainly up there as one of my biggest. Much like the game's concept, puzzles, and little three-blobbed players, the game's soundtrack may be simple at first glance, but its execution brings so much depth that I hadn't anticipated.

title: YouTuber runs onto the stage at Roblox Developers Conference shouting 'We deserve better,' gets tackled and ejected from show
event_sentences: Over the last few days, Roblox's 2026 Developers Conference was held in San Jose, California, and one of Roblox CEO David Baszucki's on-stage introduction's hit something of a hitch. Roblox YouTuber Mathieo took to the stage shouting, "We deserve better, don't we deserve better," while revealing a shirt that read "Kids deserve better," until he was quickly tackled and escorted out.

Baszucki played the incident off in the moment, saying "We all get a little excited when RDC comes along, as we just saw." But it was shared online by X user bearpuppyrbx, prompting a quote-repost from Mathieo himself—"just got kicked out #rdc26 💔," he wrote . He explained his stunt the same day in a short YouTube video uploaded to his channel.

"I know there's a lot of people that really love RDC, and I'm glad people are enjoying themselves," he said in the video. "My issue isn't with the people. I just do believe that Roblox [Corporation] isn't as dumb as they say they are … everybody's saying they don't want AI. Everybody's saying they don't want these faces messed up. Everybody wants better child safety.

Roblox's dubious child safety measures have been criticized for a number of years. It has recently introduced child accounts in an attempt to address the issue, the US Senate is actively investigating the platform , and legislation like the EU's Digital Services Act aim to force Roblox Corporation's hand in protecting minors.

The game has been called a " pedophile hellscape " by one investment firm, and Baszucki has put his foot in his mouth on this several times in the past—take, for instance, that time he suggested Roblox become a dating hub , or that disastrous interview he had with the New York Times where he suggested "the problem of predators on Roblox" was "not necessarily just as a problem, but an opportunity as well."

"We've seen that telling them just doesn't work," Mathieo said in the video. "It's been many years now where this has been a really prevalent issue. And while they're 'finding a fix,' there's probably a lot of kids that have been harmed on Roblox recently."
I have reached out to the Roblox Corporation for comment on the incident, and will update this story if I hear back.
